problem.heading:
A changed reading
needs more than one perspective.
problem.intro: A vapor trend, thermal deviation or pressure change may have several explanations. Link the right observations to the same line and operating step.

cards.title: Connections and transfer points
cards.body: Match vapor sensing to the actual substance; TVOC does not cover every gas. For water services, place contact sensors on likely spill paths. Each event directs an inspection without proving the source.

cards.title: Changing thermal or pressure duty
cards.body: Startup, cleaning and changing demand can alter pipe conditions. Compare selected temperature and pressure points with equivalent operating states before escalating a deviation.

cards.title: Airflow and adjacent machinery
cards.body: A command does not prove a valve moved or a pump delivered flow. Add the appropriate flow, position and run / fault feedback to separate an operating request from the physical result.

problem.takeaway: Associate complementary readings with a named line, equipment item and operating step so the team knows what to investigate.

focus.eyebrow: AIR POINT + PIPE POINT + OPERATING STATE
focus.heading:
Measure different quantities.
Review one operating event.
focus.intro: Give each observation its own physical meaning, then compare records from the same process period.

stages.title: Define the process concern
stages.body: Identify the medium, chemistry, equipment and operating change the team needs to investigate.

stages.title: Separate the measurement points
stages.body: Specify the gas or liquid, air location, surface contact and process port. Add a water-contact point only for confirmed compatible liquids.

stages.title: Match the time and duty
stages.body: Align readings with flow, valve-position and extraction states. Give every permitted controller command a separate equipment-feedback check.

stages.title: Investigate with the right discipline
stages.body: Operations supplies context; maintenance or EHS selects the inspection and any specialist follow-up.

focus.note: TVOC, surface temperature and pressure support investigation. They do not by themselves confirm a leak, pipe integrity or a safe atmosphere.
focus.detailTitle: How to compare different measurements responsibly
focus.detail: Use common line IDs and timestamps without treating unlike quantities as interchangeable. Pipe-wall temperature differs from fluid temperature; periodic pressure reports may miss short transients. Ambient TVOC depends on detectable compounds and airflow. Vibration requires a suitable machine point and bandwidth. Review the acquisition profile and operating state before comparing channels, and keep cause confirmation with the site’s inspection or specialist assessment process.

applications.heading:
Process-area monitoring.
From the line to its equipment.
applications.intro: The same platform can organise several measurements. The site design determines which ones are useful at each location.

faq.q: What does Smart Pipework Monitoring include?
faq.a: Select ambient TVOC or a gas-specific channel around the actual substance, then combine appropriate pipe-surface temperature, pressure and equipment data. Add water-contact points for compatible water services and external flow, valve or extraction feedback where they answer a real operating question. Sensors, instruments and control interfaces are selected separately.

faq.q: How is this different from Smart Water Monitoring?
faq.a: This page focuses on industrial process-area investigation: detectable vapors around pipework, thermal behaviour, pressure and associated equipment. Smart Water Monitoring focuses on water levels, accumulation, conveyance and supply conditions. The right category follows the operator’s task; individual sensor families may be shared.

faq.q: Can these readings confirm the source of a leak?
faq.a: They can help prioritise an investigation, but a changed trend is not source confirmation. Airflow affects ambient TVOC; pressure and temperature also change with normal operation. Use the named points and common timing to guide the site’s inspection, then record the confirmed source and any additional specialist measurements.

faq.q: Does pipe-surface temperature measure the fluid temperature?
faq.a: It measures the contact point on the pipe wall. Wall material, contact quality, insulation, ambient conditions and operating changes influence the result. Define what the surface trend should show. If the decision needs fluid temperature, specify an appropriate process probe and approved installation separately.

faq.q: Can the system provide gas safety or exposure compliance?
faq.a: Those requirements need an explicitly designed assessment or protection system. Confirm the substances, measurement method, response duty and any required certification for the exact equipment. An ambient TVOC trend and a general monitoring platform do not establish exposure compliance, %LEL coverage or an emergency shutdown function.

faq.q: What should be agreed for the multi-sensor installation?
faq.a: Agree the point layout, chemistry, probe and process interfaces, supply, acquisition profile and reporting path for every device. Keep calibration and maintenance access practical. Confirm external-system mappings and test the notification workflow, so each observation has a known meaning and an assigned response.

faq.q: Can TVOC or the water-leak sensor detect every leak?
faq.a: No. TVOC depends on the selected sensing principle and detectable substances. CH₄, H₂, NH₃, O₂ or another specific duty requires an appropriately selected channel. The water sensor detects compatible liquid reaching its sensing point; oil, solvent and low-conductivity or treated-water duties require a verified sensing method. Select the medium before specifying the detector.

faq.q: Can the controller operate valves or extraction equipment?
faq.a: HD20 can issue permitted commands through compatible equipment circuits and read available feedback; HR-10 can support approved commands through a documented instrument or equipment interface. Confirm output type, electrical rating, local priority and communication-loss behaviour. Host sequencing, interlocks and protection remain active. Emergency shutdown is not assumed to be provided by this monitoring integration.
